sentences.text: The plaintiff maintained a mutual open running current account to record transactions of all the bills raised towards the supplied made to defendants.
As per the said account, a sum of Rs.16,64,630/ is due and payable by the defendants to the plaintiff.
Since the defendants have failed and neglected to pay the aforesaid sum, they are also liable to pay interest @18% p.a. on said sum which comes to Rs.4,01,051/ till 10.04.2015.

The defendants were also liable to submit/ deposit Sales Tax/ C Forms which they failed to do, the defendants are also liable to pay a sum of Rs.3,69,106/ towards Sales Tax alongwith interest of Rs.1,20,041/ @ 2% per month till 31.03.2015.
(iii) The plaintiff issued legal demand notice dt. 20.10.2014.
Pursuant to same, defendants paid a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ to the plaintiff on 02.04.2015.
Thus, the defendants are indebted in all for a sum of Rs.25,54,828/ to the plaintiff alongwith pendente lite and future interest @18% p.a.

6.3.
Qua the said aspect, the plaintiff's case has remained unscathed, unimpeached and uncontroverted by the defendants.
There is no crossexamination of the plaintiff's witness by the defendants' side.
Necessarily, the plea that the goods supplied were not in accordance with the standards or specifications has not at all being substantiated.
Whereas, the plaintiff witness has testified to the correctness of the bills, supply of goods and receipt thereof by the defendant.

6.4. I need not add that the clearance of Sales Tax dues by the defendants also corroborates the case of the plaintiff that the sales were indeed made  the transaction consummated without any protest by the defendants.
6.5. Applicability of Arbitration Clause is also not there as thje written statement has been filed and defendant has consented to the jurisdiction of the Civil Court.

sentences.text: So far as liability of defendants is concerned, it is settled law that a company is a juristic concern.
Collectively decisions on behalf of company are taken by Board of Directors but they do not have any personal liability as such.
Same is the spirit of the Company Law as it separates the Directors from the Company.
Though viz a viz the third person the Directors may be liable as they may have dealt with them but in law, they do not have any personal liability.
As such, merely because defendant no(s) 2 and 3 were acting as Directors, would not make them liable to pay the amount as claimed by the plaintiff.
6.7. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances, the present suit is decreed in favour of the plaintiff for a principal sum of Rs.16,64,630/.
The plaintiff is also entitled to interest @12% per annum on such sum since the date of the legal notice i.e. 20.10.2014 till realization.
I have reduced the presuit interest for two reasons.
The plaintiff had also not immediately sought the balance payment but made a concrete demand through legal notice and secondly, the defendant company had cleared the outstanding Sales Tax dues.
So in the larger interest of justice, it would be apt that interest is confined accordingly.

All issues are decided accordingly in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant no. 1.
Relief 7.
In view of the findings of above said issues, this suit of the plaintiff is decreed for a sum of Rs.16,64,630/ alongwith interest @12%
